title: Sequence entropy and kernel affinity diary
content:
Objective:
Investigate how per-request sequence-length entropy in mixed workloads affects kernel-selection thrash (FlashAttention vs paged/fused ops) and resultant latency tails. Aim: find cheap heuristics to improve kernel affinity and reduce kernel-switching cost without degrading throughput or accuracy.

Context / Motivation:
- Observed intermittent 99.9th latency spikes on workloads with high sequence-length variance (chat + embeddings + long documents).
- Trace-level signals show frequent kernel handoffs within a single worker (flashpaged <-> flash fusion paths) for batches with mixed prefix lengths.
- Existing kernel-selector relies on simple percentile of seq_len in batch + model flag; seems blind to batch-internal entropy.

Quick summary of discoveries (TL;DR):
- Workloads with higher sequence-length entropy cause more kernel-switch events; each switch costs 150-400us depending on kernel priming and cached allocation state.
- Small changes (prefer single-kernel affinity for batches with entropy > 0.45) yield 6-12% reduction in 99.9 latency on our simulated mix tests, with negligible throughput loss.
- Edge case: extreme long-tail sequences (one request >> others) still causes noticeable stalls; best mitigations are prefix-padding or split scheduling.

Experiment plan (notes + commands):
1) Repro harness: sequence-mix-runner.py (local bench harness used in experiments)
- config: mixes of short (8-32), mid (64-256), long (1024-2048)
- batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16
- sampling: uniform vs Zipf(k=1.2) to control entropy

Run command (example):
PYTHONPATH=. python tools/sequence-mix-runner.py --model orca-13b --kernel-selector=prod --mix-spec mixes/zipf-k1.2.json --batch 8 --iters 1000 --trace /tmp/seq-ent-trace.log

2) Kernel-affinity probe (instrumented selector):
- Added logging to kernel_selector.cpp to emit: batch_id, seq_lengths[], entropy, chosen_kernel, kernel_switch_count, priming_cost_us
- priming_cost measured as walltime between kernel launch and first token emission for batch

Sample trace excerpt (abbreviated):
[2025-01-20T14:12:32Z] batch=142 seq=[12,16,14,13,1024,18,15,10] entropy=0.62 chosen=flashpaged->flashfusion switch=1 priming_cost=320us
[2025-01-20T14:12:32Z] batch=143 seq=[16,16,15,14,12,8,9,10] entropy=0.12 chosen=flashfusion switch=0 priming_cost=90us

Results (selected):
- Baseline (prod selector): zipf mix, batch=8
  - p50: 6.4ms, p95: 12.7ms, p99: 42.1ms, p99.9: 145.8ms
- New heuristic (entropy threshold 0.45 -> prefer single kernel choice based on median):
  - p50: 6.6ms, p95: 13.0ms, p99: 37.9ms, p99.9: 128.3ms
- Throughput difference: -1.8% observed in sustained run (loss mainly on all-short batches where fusion slightly faster).

Observations / interpretation:
- Kernel-switch cost dominates tail for mixed batches. The selector currently tries to optimally pick per-sub-batch kernel, but overhead of switching/priming is larger than suboptimal kernel execution for many cases.
- Entropy metric (Shannon on normalized seq_len categories) correlates strongly with kernel_switch_count (r=0.78 in our traces).
- Median-based single-kernel choice favors the short/mid kernel in cases where majority are short, which reduces switches and priming costs. When long sequences are many, single-kernel selection chooses long-paged path as expected.

Failure modes / caveats:
- Workloads with heavy memory pressure: when long sequences present, choosing long kernel for entire batch increases peak GPU memory and may cause OOMs; need to combine with an admission check (if estimated memory > worker_budget -> fallback to split-schedule).
- Some fused ops degrade more on short tokens per head for certain models (sparsity/reshaping overhead). We saw 3-5% perf regressions when forcing fusion aggressively for Llama-like models on A100-40GB with small KV cache footprint.

Detailed microbench notes (raw):
- priming_cost distribution (flashpaged->flashfusion handoff): mean 210us, median 180us, 95th 390us
- kernel_exec_delta (same batch if pick single non-optimal kernel): avg +28% token latency vs +320us priming overhead -> single-kernel beneficial in many mixed cases

Proposed short-term mitigations (quick wins):
- Implement entropy computation in kernel selector and add rule: if entropy > 0.45 and mem_estimate < 0.8*worker_budget then lock affinity = median_kernel for batch. (PR ready: linked_artifacts[0])
- Add per-batch memory estimation early in request pipeline to refuse affinity lock when memory risk flagged.
- Add a lightweight per-worker sticky-kernel cache that keeps last-used kernel primed for N=10 batches when same model/version to reduce priming cost for repeated patterns.

Longer-term proposals:
- Adaptive split-scheduler: split batches by bucketed seq lengths when one or two outliers exist, schedule short prefix subset on short-kernel and long tail on paged kernel. Requires cost-model for extra scheduling overhead.
- Learned kernel selector: small NN feature vector [histogram(seq_len), model_id, batch_size, recent_switches] -> kernel_plan. Offline distilled from traces.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Where to set entropy threshold? value 0.45 works on our zipf mixes, but customer mixes may differ. Plan: run sweep across production traces (sampled) next week.
- Q: How does sticky-kernel interact with autoscaling (cold nodes)? If nodes are cold, sticky helps little; need to mark cold state and adjust lock policy.
- TODO: add unit test scenarios in tracebench for single-outlier and many-outliers cases (assigned to Liam).
- TODO: schedule run against customer-beta-4 (Priya) with their chat-heavy mix; collect p99/p99.9 differences and memory telemetry.

Implementation notes and PRs:
- Changeset: kernel_selector.cc + selector_config.yaml + small runtime flag --prefer-affinity-on-entropy
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123 (experiment branch, entropy-rule toggle)
- Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, start in canary pool with low QPS models; monitor p99.9 and OOM metrics for 72h before wider rollout.

Appendix: quick pseudo-code for selector rule:
- bucketize seq_lengths into ln categories (short<=32, mid<=256, long>256)
- p = distribution over buckets, entropy = -sum(p * log(p)) / log(num_buckets)
- if entropy > T and mem_est < budget*0.8: kernel = kernel_for(median(seq_lengths)) // lock affinity
- else: fallback to existing selector (mix-aware)

Notes to self (untidy):
- We should capture per-kernel GPU resident set before/after priming to better understand the memory churn cost.
- Consider a lightweight timer on kernel-launch path for precise priming cost attribution (current walltime includes queueing jitter).
- Collect more traces from dedicated nodes (different GPU types) — observed priming cost differs across H100 vs A100.

References and links:
- tracebench scenario: tools/tracebench/scenarios/zipf-seq-mix.json
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123
- Jira: INFRA-2278 (kernel-selector entropy experiments)

Next steps (near term):
1) Run production-trace sweep and validate threshold (Ava + Diego) - target 2025-01-24
2) Add memory-estimator gating and unit tests (Liam) - target 2025-01-28
3) Canary rollout behind feature flag (Priya ops) - target 2025-02-02

If results hold, this is a cheap SLO improvement for mixed chat workloads. Document end.
